turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Price section didn't work. Too many numbers at too many sizes. Couldn't spot the total without reading every label."

We want to understand what you meant by "couldn't spot the total without reading every label", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The Total row sits at the bottom of the summary card with no visual separation from the Subtotal and Shipping rows above it, so it doesn't stand out as the final figure.

B) The Total label is bold but its corresponding value ($288.99) appears at the same size as the Subtotal value directly above it, making the two figures visually indistinguishable at a glance.

C) The order summary card has no dedicated section break or dividing line between the line-item prices ($249.00, $39.99) and the totalling rows (Subtotal, Shipping, Total), so all numbers sit in one undifferentiated block.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.

Looking at the Total row specifically, the label "Total" is bold but the $288.99 value to its right appears the same size as the $288.99 directly above it in the Subtotal row — is it the value's size, its weight, or its position on the right side that you'd expect to signal "this is the final number"?
turns.a: Subtotal, tax, total — all different sizes. No obvious main number. Couldn't tell which was the total at a glance.

turns.q: If someone arrived at this layout just before entering their card details, would not immediately recognising the Total figure cause them to pause before filling in the Payment Details section — or would it only become a problem later?

turns.q: If the $288.99 Total value matched the bold weight of its label — without changing anything else in this layout — would that be enough to let you confirm the total at a glance, or is there something about how the rows are arranged that would still make you stop and read?
